title: Solve the exact independent random-horizon tradeoff by convexity
statement: For d>=2,u=(d-1)/d^2,a(t)=1-2u(1-cos t), delta(d,n)=d/(2pi) integral_0^pi[1-a(t)^n]/[n(1-cos t)]dt extends strictly decreasing and strictly convex to all real n>0. For0<a<1, (1-a^n)/n=(-log a) integral_0^1 a^(nv)dv; a=0 uses1/n. For integer K>=0 independent of BOTH entire source streams INCLUDING actual X, exact Q^m conditional on every K and conditional caps K fresh P,m+K fresh Q, the exact smallest WORST-CASE excess is E delta(d,m+K), attained by the archive at each horizon. Jensen gives >=delta(d,m+E K), and at a prescribed real mean the optimum integer law is supported on the adjacent integers. Heavy-tailed independent horizons do not improve this frontier; adaptive observation-selected horizons and mixture-only exactness are excluded. Exact delta(d,n)=d sum_(a,b<=n)|a-b|binom(n,a)binom(n,b)(d-1)^(2n-a-b)/(2n d^(2n)) permits finite integer search for N_min. With N_max=max(m,ceil((d-1)/(2eta^2))), expected bit work O((N_max+d+B+1)^8), stated paid list/counter memory, and delta(d,n)~sqrt((d-1)/(pi n)) as n tends to infinity with d FIXED; N_min(d,m,eta)~(d-1)/(pi eta^2) as eta tends to zero with BOTH d and m FIXED. No binary-input polynomial or unrestricted minimax solution.
